title: Coefficients pulled back from the point
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, that is, a
condensed ring ([det-def-sfb-ring-object]). For a scheme $X$, put
$$
\Lambda_X:=p_X^*\Lambda\in\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),
$$
where $p_X^*$ is the inverse image from the point
([det-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]).

The ring object structure is transported along the strong monoidal functor
$p_X^*$. The unit is $\Z\cong p_X^*\Z\to p_X^*\Lambda$. The multiplication is
$$
p_X^*\Lambda\otimes p_X^*\Lambda\cong p_X^*(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)\to p_X^*\Lambda .
$$
This makes $\Lambda_X$ a ring object of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, and
$\Lambda\mapsto\Lambda_X$ is a functor from ring objects of
$\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ to ring objects of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$.
If $\Lambda$ is commutative, then so is $\Lambda_X$.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line per clause: take F=p_X^*, with its strong monoidal braided structure supplied by det-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, between the two abelian-sheaf tensor categories of det-def-sfb-ring-object. CategoryTheory.Functor.mapMon, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mon.lean:867–869, is the required functor on ring objects (Mon objects), sending Lambda to F.obj Lambda and a ring morphism phi to F.map phi.hom. The induced ring structure is CategoryTheory.Functor.monObjObj at Mon.lean:827–836: one := epsilon F followed by F.map eta, mul := LaxMonoidal.mu F Lambda Lambda followed by F.map mu. These are exactly the two displayed maps of the item, as also recorded by CategoryTheory.Functor.obj.η_def at line 844 and obj.μ_def at line 847. CategoryTheory.Functor.map.instIsMonHom at Mon.lean:850–852 supplies preservation of unit and multiplication for morphisms. For the final clause apply CategoryTheory.Functor.isCommMonObj_obj, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/CommMon_.lean:157–159; its F.LaxBraided hypothesis follows from the given braided strong monoidal structure. CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCommMon at CommMon_.lean:169–176 packages the same commutative construction. Read Mon.lean:73–84 and 815–875, CommMon_.lean:146–176. MonObj is precisely the ring-object convention of the statement (tensor over Z, sheafified on the sites), not a cartesian ring object. All operations use the supplied monoidal comparison maps, with exactly the stated direction. This does not construct p_X^* or assert its monoidality independently: those data remain the existing statement dependency. No commutativity is required for the first clauses, and no finiteness, nonemptiness or other new hypothesis on X or Lambda is used.
